title: Chapter 4 Quiz 10
description: Traps in every question. Trace each loop one pass at a time.
instructions: Chapter 4: Difficult: arrays, sorting and traces.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: This should display the product of the 5 elements of tab. Two lines have an error.
questions.code:
Declare tab [1..5] : ARRAY OF integer
Let product ← 0
For i From 1 To 5 Do
    product ← product + tab[i]
EndFor
Display(product)
questions.explanation: Line 2: a product must start at 1. Line 4: we must multiply, not add. Watch out: starting at 0 would make the product 0 even with the right operator, and the wrong operator gives the sum.

questions.question: Sort [29, 10, 14, 37, 13] with selection sort. Give the array after each pass.
questions.explanation: Each pass swaps the smallest remaining value into position i. Watch out: pass 3 swaps 14 with 13, and pass 4 makes a swap too, even though the order is already right after it.

questions.question: How many swaps does bubble sort make in total on [5, 1, 4, 2, 8]?
questions.explanation: Pass 1 makes 3 swaps (5 passes 1, 4, 2), pass 2 makes 1 swap (4 and 2), and passes 3 and 4 make none: 4 swaps. Watch out: we count swaps, not comparisons (that would be 10).

questions.question: This should give the exact average of the 5 values, with decimals. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Let sum ← 0
For i From 1 To 5 Do
    sum ← sum + tab[i]
EndFor
Let average ← sum DIV 5
Display(average)
questions.explanation: The / operator gives the real division. Watch out: DIV drops the decimals, and MOD gives the remainder.

questions.question: In the minimum search on [15, 7, 22, 3, 19], starting with min ← tab[1], how many times is min replaced by a smaller value?
questions.explanation: min changes at 7 and at 3: 2 times. Watch out: the first assignment min ← tab[1] is not a replacement, and 22 and 19 are not smaller.

questions.question: What is the array after pass 2 of selection sort on [9, 4, 7, 1]?
questions.explanation: Pass 1 swaps 9 with 1: 1 4 7 9. Pass 2 finds that 4 is already the smallest of the rest, so nothing changes. Watch out: a pass can leave the array as it is.

questions.question: Delete position 1 of [5, 6, 7, 8]. Give the array after each shift.
questions.explanation: Each value moves one place left. The last cell still holds 8, but the new size is 3. Watch out: the shifts start at pos, so the first shift copies 6 over 5.

questions.question: Selection sort makes exactly one swap per pass, even when the smallest value is already in place.
questions.explanation: The algorithm always swaps tab[i] with tab[minIndex]; if they are the same cell nothing changes. Watch out: a swap does not always move something.

questions.question: Which of these statements are **true**?
options: A sum can start at any value
Deleting a value shifts others left
The index is the stored value too
questions.explanation: [0..9] has 10 cells, deleting shifts the next values left, and consecutive indexes are neighbouring cells. Watch out: the index is the position and the value is the content, and a sum must start at 0.

questions.assertion: Starting a minimum search with min ← 0 always works.
questions.reason: No element of an array can be smaller than 0.
questions.explanation: Both are false: when all values are positive, 0 stays the minimum and is not in the array, and negative values exist. Watch out: 0 looks like a safe starting value, but the first element is the safe one.

questions.question: This bubble sort compares neighbours, and one line reads outside the array on the first pass. Find it and type the corrected line.
questions.code:
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    For j From 1 To 5 - i Do
        If tab[j] > tab[j - 1] Then
            Swap(tab[j], tab[j + 1])
        EndIf
    EndFor
EndFor
questions.explanation: The pair compared must be the one that is swapped: tab[j] and tab[j + 1]. Watch out: tab[j - 1] is tab[0] on the first pass, and it does not exist.
